text:
Maya: quick thought — saw a p99 shift after the kernel selector change on dedicated nodes, want to prototype a tiny traffic generator to reproduce the shape locally
Leo: +1. can you sketch inputs?
Maya: name: eddyflow. goal: combine a slow ramp, jittered microbursts, and controlled KV cold/warm phases. try to avoid full-blown replay, keep it parametric so we can sweep heuristics
Arjun: sounds good. important to isolate batching effects vs kernel choice. suggest we run identical model binary with different kernel selection flags for apples-to-apples
Nina: also need to vary KV hitrate — i.e., percentage of requests that hit prefix cache vs cold start. that seemed correlated with the regression
Kai: would be nice to emit perf counters and a tiny profile snapshot on each run (cpu/gpu kerntime, kernel name, batch sizes produced). bench-bot can stash artifacts to s3
Maya: prototype config (rough):
```
qps_profile: 
  - start: 10
    end: 80
    duration_s: 180
microburst: 
  rate: 400
  chance_per_sec: 0.04
kv_phase: 
  - warm_pct: 90
    duration_s: 120
  - warm_pct: 20
    duration_s: 60
seed: random
metrics: [latency_hist, kernel_name, batch_distribution, kv_hit]
```
Leo: nice, add a 'stutter' option where we inject short tails of high seq_len requests to stress kv cache growth behavior
Arjun: for apples-to-apples we need to pin everything: same hw, same model weights, same concurrency limit. Only flip kernel flags and batching heuristic binary parameter (auto vs fixed)
Nina: agree. what about replay harness? i think eddyflow should generate synthetic bursts but we can add a replay mode that replays a day's worth of sampled requests for verification
Kai: bench-bot: run plan?
bench-bot: scheduled eddyflow-run-1 on infra-testing-03 (gpu-a100) with tags [eddyflow, kernel-audit]. artifacts -> s3://redwood-perf/eddyflow/3732109876/
Maya: great. postmortem checklist: 1) compare p50/p95/p99 across kernel variants, 2) plot batch size distribution over time, 3) KV hitrate vs latency buckets, 4) attach flamegraphs for any regressions
Leo: if we see p99 shifts only when kv warm_pct < 30% that hints at cache eviction behavior + kernel path mismatch
Arjun: and if batch-size distribution shifts toward smaller batches during bursts, check batching heuristic thresholds — maybe the change reduced wait-window for coalescing
Nina: also capture memory alloc patterns — sometimes quantized kernels allocate more scratch memory leading to longer kernel launch times under pressure
Kai: i'll add a small telemetry collector to the harness to capture kernel names and their per-call durations; want to correlate with sequence lengths too
Maya: ok i'll push a minimal repo + readme and link here when ready. goal: reproduce regression with eddyflow and make a small test that guards against it in CI
Leo: awesome—if you want i can help with the plotting scripts (CDFs + sliding-window p99)
Maya: thanks! expecting first run artifacts in ~30m
bench-bot: run completed. logs+plots uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/eddyflow/3732109876/results.zip (status: success) :rocket:
